# tu 1.1.3 — rename sessions, update with one key

## What's new since `v1.1.2`

- **Rename a session.** Press **r** (or click **Rename**) on a session:
  a small modal opens with the current name already in the field.
  Enter runs `tmux rename-session`; the renamed row stays selected.
  Names follow tmux's rules (no `:` or `.`, no leading/trailing
  spaces) and the modal says what's wrong while you type; a duplicate
  is refused before tmux is called.
- **Update with one key.** When the status row says a newer release
  exists, press **u** or click the note. The Update modal shows how
  `tu` was installed and the exact command it will run; Enter closes
  `tu`, runs it with the terminal attached (sudo can prompt), and
  exits so the next launch is the new version. Supported methods:
  Homebrew (`brew upgrade tu`), cargo (`cargo install tmux-tu`),
  install.sh / tarball (re-runs install.sh into the same directory),
  `.deb` (`sudo dpkg -i`) and `.rpm` (`sudo rpm -U`).
- **`tu --update`** does the same from the shell;
  **`tu --check-update`** only checks and prints the verdict, exiting
  0 / 10 / 11 for up to date / update available / unreachable.
- **Leaner bottom row.** The hint bar is gone; each button carries its
  own shortcut in yellow (**N**ew, **A**ttach, **R**ename, **D**etach,
  Cancel **Esc**, Delete **Bksp**). Six buttons fit an 80-column pane.
- **Fix:** modal bodies were one row short, which hid the last line
  (the Delete modal's "This cannot be undone." was never visible).

## Upgrading from 1.1.2

1.1.2 shows the "newer release" note but cannot update itself yet.
Upgrade once by hand with the method you installed with
(`brew upgrade tu`, `cargo install tmux-tu`, re-run install.sh, or
the package below). From 1.1.3 on, **u** does it.

## Install

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hungryZoo/tu/main/install.sh | sh
```

Homebrew: `brew install hungryZoo/tap/tu` · crates.io: `cargo install tmux-tu` ·
packages and tarballs are attached below, with `SHA256SUMS`.
